diagnosis.root_cause: Two RADIUS radcheck rows exist for the same username, with conflicting lineids. The orphan lineid does not match any active CRM customer, causing FreeRADIUS to resolve the records inconsistently and repeatedly re-authenticate the subscriber.
evidence: The subscriber has 19 sessions in 24 hours and 118 in seven days, far above the normal 2-3 sessions per day baseline.
Average session duration is only 38 minutes versus the normal 11.9 hours, confirming repeated session interruption.
The ONU is online and responding, with RX power -20.58 dBm and TX power 2.45 dBm, both within normal EPON ranges.
Seven-day RX and TX telemetry is stable and within the healthy optical noise floor; distance is constant at 96, so fiber degradation, laser degradation, and distance change are unsupported.
All sampled ONUs on EPON0/5 are online and healthy, the OLT is responsive, and OLT CPU, memory, and temperature are normal, ruling out ONU, PON-port, OLT, and router faults.
The customer VLAN is present and correctly mapped to VLAN 1055, ruling out stuck provisioning or VLAN 46 issues.

RADIUS contains two rows for the same username, one with the correct CRM lineid and one orphan row with lineid 1C:EF:03:90:2B:5A; FreeRADIUS may select either row, directly explaining the authentication flapping.

remediation.action: Remove the orphan radcheck row for username 30:16:9D:A2:5F:03, retain the row containing lineid 00:A1:07:C4:1D:88, and reconcile the RADIUS record with CRM. Flush any cached authentication state and terminate the conflicting active sessions so the subscriber can establish one clean session. Monitor re-authentication counts and session duration afterward.

ground_truth.root_cause: Two radcheck rows exist for the same username. FreeRADIUS resolves inconsistently between them, so authentication succeeds or fails depending on which row is matched, producing repeated short sessions and two alternating IP assignments.
expected_reasoning: 19 sessions in 24h against a 2-3 baseline, with a 38 minute mean duration against an 11.9 hour norm
RX has been flat at -20.6 dBm for seven days inside the +/-0.3 dBm noise floor, so signal is not the cause
TX power, bias current, supply voltage and distance are all stable
Port neighbours are normal and the OLT is healthy, so no shared infrastructure fault
With no optical explanation available, the search moves to the authentication layer
RADIUS holds two radcheck rows for username 30:16:9D:A2:5F:03, one of them an orphan with a different lineid
Recent sessions alternate between two IP addresses, consistent with inconsistent row resolution
Traffic is erratic rather than declining, which fits intermittent authentication rather than a degrading link

expected_escalation.review_reason: Duplicate RADIUS rows must be resolved by hand; deleting the wrong row disconnects the customer

distractors: The session pattern is identical to signal-related flapping and invites that diagnosis
Zero-throughput windows in the speed series look like link loss but coincide with rejected auth
ONU is a Router type, inviting a CPE-fault explanation
